stem: What is the main reason a grommet may be used in otitis media with effusion?

options.text: It breaks the suction of negative middle ear pressure
It predicts the type of middle ear fluid
It replaces the need for hearing assessment
It is routinely required in every case of otitis media with effusion

explanation: Grommets relieve negative middle ear pressure by breaking the suction in the middle ear, which helps ventilation.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

rationale: The correct concept is mechanical pressure relief in otitis media with effusion, not prediction of fluid type or routine use in every case.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a grommet ventilates the middle ear and breaks the suction of negative pressure.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because grommets do not predict the nature of the middle ear fluid.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because otitis media with effusion does not by itself confirm long-term language impairment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a grommet does not replace the need for hearing assessment.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because grommets are not routinely required in every case of otitis media with effusion.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
